speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML. Full_Blood_Count: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That history is very concerning for Multiple Sclerosis, especially given your use of natalizumab. To confirm the diagnosis and check for treatment-related risks, please look at the MRI_Brain and Full_Blood_Count results I ordered and let me know what they show. Additionally, do you have any personal history of seizures or other neurological episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. The patient's history of Crohn's disease treated with natalizumab, combined with new onset gait ataxia, limb weakness, and the absence of fever or infection, strongly suggests JC virus reactivation. Immediate discontinuation of natalizumab and confirmation via MRI findings of white matter lesions without mass effect or contrast enhancement are required.
